variables.name: Purpose Alignment
questions: What outcome is this role ultimately responsible for?
Which stakeholder must experience the value?
What work is performed mainly because the process exists?
Which decision would this role stop making if purpose were clearer?
What evidence shows the role is creating the intended outcome?

variables.name: Pressure Load
questions: Which demand changes most often?
What creates the largest queue or delay?
Which deadline carries the greatest consequence?
What happens when workload doubles?
Which external pressure could make current practice fail?

variables.name: Human Capacity
questions: Which human strengths are essential to this work?
Where is attention regularly overloaded?
Which skills are concentrated in one person?
What work pattern helps this role perform at its best?
Which tasks create avoidable fatigue or cognitive switching?

variables.name: AI Fit
questions: Which tasks are repeatable and evidence-rich?
Which tasks require contextual or ethical judgement?
How reversible is an incorrect AI-supported decision?
Where could AI prepare options without making the decision?
What must always remain under accountable human authority?

variables.name: Authority Clarity
questions: Who may approve the output?
Who is accountable when the recommendation is wrong?
Who may override or appeal the decision?
Which authority is assumed but not documented?
What decision is delayed because ownership is unclear?

variables.name: Artefact Integrity
questions: Which documents or data are required before work can begin?
Which artefact is most often missing, stale or contradictory?
Where is provenance recorded?
Which output becomes an input for another role?
What evidence must survive onboarding, handover and offboarding?

variables.name: Flow and Tempo
questions: How quickly must this role respond?
Where does work wait rather than progress?
How many handoffs occur before completion?
Which interruptions cause the most rework?
What tempo would be unsafe even if technically possible?

variables.name: Dependency Resilience
questions: Which role, system or supplier can stop this work?
What substitute exists if that dependency fails?
Which dependency is poorly understood?
How quickly can the role recover after interruption?
Where would one failure cascade across the organisation?

variables.name: Learning and Memory
questions: How does this role learn whether an action worked?
Where are failures and exceptions recorded?
Which knowledge disappears when a person leaves?
How are successful adaptations selected and reused?
What feedback arrives too late to improve the next cycle?

variables.name: Trust and Flourishing
questions: Who could be helped or harmed by this work?
What would make employees or customers distrust the system?
Does the proposed change improve meaningful human contribution?
What hidden cost or externality is not in the KPI?
How will affected people understand and challenge the outcome?
